reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is a Litecoin Summit presentation about crypto adoption and Beluga's proposed role as a discovery and information platform for crypto products. Remarks about people buying Bitcoin for potential profit and lists of new tokens or projects are presented as industry analysis and product strategy rather than a guaranteed-return solicitation. The described material does not show a required payment, credential request, false affiliation, deceptive outcome, or specific transaction being solicited.

citations.quote: we launched Beluga which is kind of a nerd wall or credit karma for crypto
to be a platform where we reveal and find the best products in crypto
we write these great product reviews, about new products that are launching

opening.argument: Judge, consider the sequence presented to a prospective user: people hear “I can get rich. I can make money” and buy Bitcoin; Beluga then identifies “the hot new token to buy” as what draws people in. Its response is a ranked list of new projects, followed by an effort to bring those visitors onto the site. That connects a wealth-oriented reason for purchasing crypto to a practical way of finding purchases. The speaker does not personally guarantee a return, but the purchase pathway is central to the pitch, not incidental market background.

citations.quote: they hear about hey I can get rich. I can make money so I'm gonna buy some Bitcoin and Robinhood
what's the hot new token to buy
We create a top 50 list of the top new projects that are launching, that are backed by tier-one VCs and all that
that gets you coming to the site

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls Beluga a discovery platform, but discovery is the mechanism for steering a purchase-minded audience: the speaker says the token list gets people to the site. Product reviews do not erase that initial appeal. The absence of a required payment in the presentation is a narrower point than whether the presentation promotes a route from interest in gains to token selection.

citations.quote: what's the hot new token to buy
that gets you coming to the site

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The wealth language describes why other people buy and then stop using crypto; the speaker presents that behavior as the problem. The token list is described as an entry point for showing visitors other products. Neither quote promises that a listed token will appreciate or asks viewers to buy one.

citations.quote: they hear about hey I can get rich. I can make money so I'm gonna buy some Bitcoin and Robinhood or whatever and I sit there and look at it go
we give them what they want first and then start trying to make them smarter now about other products and crypto

opening.argument: Judge, the concern is the combination of signals, not any single phrase. The speaker says users chiefly care about the next token to buy, offers a top-50 list of new projects described as backed by tier-one VCs, and acknowledges uncertainty about whether its reported follower count represents real people. Together, those details put purchase interest, apparent institutional credibility, and audience-size credibility in the same promotional presentation. The cited backing is a claim about the projects, not evidence here that buying them will pay off; that gap matters when the list is presented to people looking for a token to buy.

citations.quote: what's the hot new token to buy. That's all anyone cares about in crypto.
We create a top 50 list of the top new projects that are launching, that are backed by tier-one VCs
we have 165,000 Twitter followers. Which isn't really lot in crypto. But that's more than Credit Karma and NerdWall combined.
who knows how many of them are bots or real anyways

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to reviews and the lack of an explicit transaction. But a ranked list aimed at people seeking a new token to buy can influence purchases without processing one onstage. Nor does calling the site a discovery platform resolve what viewers are meant to infer from the claim that listed projects have tier-one VC backing.

citations.quote: We create a top 50 list of the top new projects that are launching, that are backed by tier-one VCs and all that
to be a platform where we reveal and find the best products in crypto

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are disclosed aspects of a product pitch, not proof of a deceptive investment offer. The speaker expressly questions the reliability of the follower figure, while the stated aim is to review and explain crypto products. No cited passage promises appreciation for a listed project or directs viewers to buy it.

citations.quote: who knows how many of them are bots or real anyways
we write these great product reviews, about new products that are launching
the site is meant for those 500 million people to start understanding more about the crypto they own and what they can do with it.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also serves a promotional funnel. Beluga presents itself as a trusted showcase of the best crypto projects, while the speaker says the draw is what people already want: a hot new token to buy. Once visitors arrive, the plan is to show them other products and build trust with the community. This is more than a detached explanation of adoption trends; it is a presentation of how a branded site attracts purchase-oriented users and steers what they consider next. The claimed trustworthiness is part of that persuasion, not independent verification of any project's prospects.

citations.quote: what's the hot new token to buy. That's all anyone cares about in crypto. So we give them what they want.

once they're on our site we're gonna say, oh, by the way, here's some great new procs that by the way here's some great new parts that are launching here some great new web3 games you might want to play
once we make them a trusted user from our community

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately identifies the stated review and discovery functions, but those functions are also how the site draws and retains users. The speaker explicitly says it gives people what they want first, then directs their attention to other crypto products. A presentation can explain a business model and promote participation at the same time; the review framing alone does not settle how to read that invitation.

citations.quote: we give them what they want first and then start trying to make them smarter now about other products and crypto
to be a platform where we reveal and find the best products in crypto

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of Beluga does not itself establish a scam. The described destination offers product discovery and reviews, and the speaker's stated goal is to help existing crypto owners understand uses beyond buying and holding. The argument identifies no false project claim, promised token gain, or requested investment in the presentation.
